original_question: Let λ be a strong limit singular cardinal that is not a limit of measurable cardinals. Is it consistent that for every cardinal µ with λ < µ ≤ 2^λ, every 2-coloring of µ×λ has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes µ and λ; equivalently, does \( inom{\mu}{\lambda} 	o  inom{\mu}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2\) hold throughout the whole interval (λ, 2^λ]?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It has the same hypothesis on λ (a strong limit singular cardinal that is not a limit of measurable cardinals), the same consistency form, the same full interval of cardinals μ with λ < μ ≤ 2^λ, and the same 2-color strong polarized relation. This matches Problem 4.12 rather than the narrower endpoint questions in Problems 4.6 and 4.7.
missing_details: To make it fully stand-alone, it is best to unpack the arrow notation formally: for every coloring c: μ×λ→2, there exist A⊆μ and B⊆λ with |A|=μ and |B|=λ such that c restricted to A×B is constant.
The paper presents this specifically as a spectral problem, i.e. simultaneous positivity for all μ in the interval (λ, 2^λ], not just the endpoint cases μ=λ^+ and μ=2^λ.
refined_question: Let λ be a strong limit singular cardinal that is not a limit of measurable cardinals. Is it consistent that for every cardinal μ with λ < μ ≤ 2^λ and every coloring c: μ×λ→2, there exist sets A⊆μ and B⊆λ such that |A|=μ, |B|=λ, and c is constant on A×B?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is it consistent that for every cardinal μ in the interval (λ, 2^λ], one has \binom{\mu}{\lambda} \to \binom{\mu}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2?
justification: The exact paper target is Problem 4.12, which asks verbatim for the consistency of the full spectrum μ∈(λ,2^λ] satisfying the strong polarized relation when λ is a strong limit singular cardinal not a limit of measurable cardinals. Definition 1.1 gives the precise meaning of the arrow notation. The immediately preceding Problems 4.6 and 4.7 isolate the two endpoint cases μ=λ^+ and μ=2^λ, so your interval formulation is correctly aiming at the broader spectrum question rather than those neighboring special cases. The introduction, Proposition 1.2, and especially Theorem 5.1 with Corollary 5.3 provide the nearby context: the paper develops general positive results for pairs (μ,λ) under extra pcf/forcing hypotheses and notes that under extra assumptions one can obtain a positive answer, while the general strong-limit-singular case remains open.
